dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the terminology list and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The clinic roster review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I can interpret a short follow-up call without vocal fatigue.
That is a bounded exchange.
It does not require continuous teaching voice.
Someone new shadowed me in the interpretation hub this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the specialty clinics into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
On 15 January, I led one 50-minute rehearsal after trainees reviewed the terminology list for the cardiology clinic.
How did Friday's transplant-family consultation go?
My interpretation remained steady through the full appointment.
I prepare trainees with a bilingual terminology list and silent video captions.
Can the group review those before practice?
Yes, then the live session can be much shorter.
I archived last cycle's notes on the clinic roster and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
You volunteered at a community forum all afternoon.
I rotated with other interpreters and did not have a high-stakes clinic booked next morning.
It was not continuous solo speech.
A vendor call about the terminology list ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the interpretation hub checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the specialty clinics.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the clinic roster records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
On 27 February, I repeated a pediatric role-play three times before a 08:00 transplant consultation.
What happened in clinic?
My voice was too weak for long family questions, so the backup interpreter stepped in.
I sketched next week's plan for the specialty clinics before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the terminology list updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
I am recovering from a vocal-cord inflammation, and the ENT has asked for longer quiet intervals between sustained sessions.
Is an asynchronous review viable?
Yes, the captioned video and terminology list are ready.
I compared two options for the clinic roster tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the interpretation hub handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
Should I rank a full Thursday role-play above a terminology-list review and one short practice before Friday's transplant consultation?
